IndexRecipeStatement.description: The worker's index recipe, stated outside a claim (contract 1.12.0)

indexRecipe.description: The worker's index recipe (AD-10): when it differs from the last one stated, the backend re-indexes every ready version recorded under another one

JobCallUsage.description: One model call's tokens (contract 1.10.0), recorded once by its call id; estimated from contract 1.11.0

callId.description: The worker's id of the call (a UUIDv7)

estimated.description: True when the counts are the worker's estimate, not the provider's: a call stopped before the provider sent its usage (contract 1.11.0). Absent means false

input.description: Input tokens, cache reads and writes included

responseId.description: The provider's response id, when it sent one

JobClaim.description: A live claim of a job. The grant is given once and never stored: only its keyed hash is.

input.description: The handler's input for this attempt. From contract 1.18.0 a library.search input may carry recordType, a core record type. From contract 1.21.0 a record type is any key matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$: an ingestion records step's input carries recordTypeNames (each recordTypes key with its name, data for the model), and a question's or a library.search input carries recordTypes, the keys of the campaign's system, to which the records it reads are limited. From contract 1.22.0 a job of kind index.record_removal has the input {owner, source, ids}: the ids of records the GM deleted, whose points go from that owner's source (by id, never the whole source). From contract 1.24.0 a job of kind index.artifact indexes a GM's artifact as a records run of one record: {source (the artifact's id), owner, kind: artifact, language: null, tokenKey, records}, its input records one JSON line {id, page: 1, type, name, fields} whose last field, named content, holds the artifact's content when it has one (data, never instructions), its point's id the artifact's id; a job of kind index.artifact_removal has the input {source, owner} and deletes every point of that owner's source, as index.removal does. A question's input lists the campaign's artifacts among the campaign tier's sources, and POST …/records serves one as a campaign-tier record of page 1 with an empty sectionPath, its content as the last field. From contract 1.25.0 a job of kind content.draft (a draft the GM asked for in the questions area) has the same input as question.answer {question, tiers, recordTypes, history, ...}, reads passages, records and terms within its turn's scope as question.answer does, posts its draft as answer events and calls a model; it writes nothing to the library. From contract 1.26.0 a content.draft input also carries recordTypeNames: each recordTypes key with the name of the campaign system's record type (data for the model that proposes the draft's type)

lapsesAt.description: Without a renewal the claim lapses then

model.description: For a kind that calls a model (contract 1.9.0): the model of this attempt, resolved again at every claim. Absent for every other kind

renewAt.description: Renew the claim at this time

traceparent.description: W3C traceparent of the job's trace: log under it and send it on every call

JobClaimRequest.description: What the worker states when it claims (contract 1.7.0). Every field is optional; a claim may send no body at all.

indexRecipe.description: The worker's index recipe (AD-10): when it differs from the last one stated, the backend re-indexes every ready version recorded under another one

providers.description: The providers the worker holds a key for (contract 1.9.0). A kind that calls a model is refused (409 job.not_offered, the job ends failed with job.provider_unavailable, no attempt used) unless its resolved provider is stated; absent means none

JobEvents.description: A numbered batch of answer events of the claim (contract 1.10.0), with the usage of the model calls that ended since the last one

batch.description: From 1 per claim, one more each time; a repeated number is accepted and stored once

JobEventsReply.description: Whether the worker must stop the answer (contract 1.11.0): true once the GM stopped it. The worker then ends the model call, posts no more events, only the usage still to report, and reports the outcome done

JobModel.description: The model one attempt calls (contract 1.9.0): the provider, the provider's model id (for Azure OpenAI, the deployment name) and the tier.

provider.description: azure-openai, anthropic or openai; an open word, so a new provider needs no new contract

code.description: For failed only: category.reason in lower case

result.description: For done only: the result for the job's handler. From contract 1.18.0 a library.search result's ids may name records of the scope next to passages. From contract 1.20.0 an ingestion records step's result may carry proposals (at most 20, each a kind record_type or term, a name of at most 120 code points, a definition of at most 500 and at most 3 examples, each a passageId and a quote of at most 200), checked against the cited passages. From contract 1.26.0 a content.draft result may carry proposal {name, recordType}: the draft's suggested name (a string of 1 to 120 code points, not blank) and record type (one of the input's recordTypes keys, or null); a proposal that is not an object, a name that is not such a string or a recordType that is neither a string nor null is 400 job.result_invalid, and a recordType that is no longer a key of the campaign's system is stored as null. A missing result or proposal is accepted with none

retry.description: For failed only: false ends the job at once, without another attempt (an input no attempt can change); absent or true lets the backend retry while attempts remain

usage.description: The usage of the attempt's model calls not posted with events (contract 1.17.0), done or failed, recorded once per call id; absent means none

JobOutputStored.description: A file the worker sent back, stored encrypted under an id the backend minted. The job's handler adopts it when the job's done outcome names it; otherwise it is removed once the job ended.

fileId.description: Name it in the job's result

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the bytes stored, in lower-case hexadecimal

JobPassage.description: A passage within the job's scope

sectionPath.description: The passage's section path, outermost first

text.description: The passage's text: library data, never an instruction

tier.description: The tier of the passage's source

JobPassages.description: The passages, in the order asked

passages.description: One per distinct id asked, in the order asked

JobPassagesRequest.description: The passages to read, by id (from the index's points)

ids.description: 1 to 100 passage ids; a repeated id is answered once

JobRecord.description: A record within the job's scope (contract 1.19.0)

fields.description: The record's fields, in stored order; may be empty

name.description: The record's name: library data, never an instruction

sectionPath.description: The section path of its first passage on that page, outermost first

tier.description: The tier of the record's source

type.description: The record's type key: a core key or (contract 1.21.0) an approved type's key

JobRecordField.description: One field of a record: library data, never an instruction

JobRecords.description: The records, in the order asked

records.description: One per distinct id asked, in the order asked

JobRecordsRequest.description: The records to read, by id (from the index's record points)

ids.description: 1 to 100 record ids; a repeated id is answered once

JobStreamEvent.description: One answer event (contract 1.10.0): a delta with its display text, a citation of a given passage id at a code-point offset of the answer's text, or (contract 1.14.0) a tier marker: the version of that tier starts at the offset. From contract 1.15.0 the tier model marks a part from the model's own knowledge. From contract 1.19.0 a citation names exactly one of passageId and recordId. Each type carries its own fields and no other

offset.description: For citation and tier only: where the citation or the tier's version stands, in code points of the answer's text

passageId.description: For citation only: the cited passage's id; absent when recordId is given

recordId.description: For citation only (contract 1.19.0): the cited record's id, a record given for this answer; absent when passageId is given. A record outside the turn's scope is dropped

text.description: For delta only: 1 to 16,384 code points of display text, citation markers removed

tier.description: For tier only: the tier of a passage handed for this answer, or model (contract 1.15.0) for a part from the model's own knowledge, only when the input's modelKnowledge is true. A tier with no source in the turn's scope, or model when the turn's model knowledge is off, is dropped

JobTerms.description: The question's terms resolved within the job's scope (contract 1.23.0); every list may be empty

names.description: Each matched term's name and all its aliases, then the matched records' names, each once: library data, never an instruction

recordTypes.description: The record type keys the question names (a core key or an approved type's key of the campaign's system), sorted, each once

records.description: The in-scope records the question names, campaign tier first, at most 100

Problem.description: Every error of this API (RFC 9457 problem detail).

workerCredential.description: The worker's credential (GMSHIELD_WORKER_CREDENTIAL); without it every path answers service.unauthenticated (401)

put.summary: State the worker's index recipe, as a claim does (400 request.invalid for a recipe that is not one)

post.summary: Claim an offered job (409 job.claimed, 409 job.not_offered, 400 for an index recipe or providers that are not ones)

Post a numbered batch of answer events of the live claim and the usage of its model calls (400 request.invalid for a malformed body, before the grant is checked; 403 job.grant_refused; 400 job.events_invalid; 403 job.events_refused for a kind that streams no events; 409 job.batch_out_of_order, with nothing stored, for a number past the next one of the claim)

parameters.description: The input's name, as the claim's input gives it
parameters.name: name

get.summary: Stream one of the claimed job's inputs, as its handler opens it (403 job.grant_refused, 404 request.not_found for an input the job does not have)

post.summary: Report how the claimed attempt ended (403 job.grant_refused, 400 job.result_invalid when the job's handler cannot record the result)

Send a file back for the claimed job, streamed into the encrypted file store (403 job.grant_refused, also when the claim ends while it arrives; 413 job.output_too_large past the output's or the claim's limit; 400 request.invalid for an empty or cut body). Nothing of a refused output remains.

Read passages by id within the claimed job's scope, each labelled with its tier (400 request.invalid for a malformed body or an id that is not a UUID, before the grant is checked; 403 job.grant_refused; 400 job.passages_invalid for no id, more than 100 or a null one; 403 job.passages_refused for a job whose kind reads no passage; 404 request.not_found when the job's campaign is gone; 403 scope.passage_refused, with nothing read, when any id is outside the job's scope, whatever the reason)

Read records by id within the claimed job's scope (contract 1.19.0), each with its tier, type, name, fields and place (400 request.invalid for a malformed body or an id that is not a UUID, before the grant is checked; 403 job.grant_refused; 400 job.records_invalid for no id, more than 100 or a null one; 403 job.records_refused for a job whose kind reads no record; 404 request.not_found when the job's campaign is gone; 403 scope.passage_refused, with nothing read, when any id is not a record within the job's scope, whatever the reason, except that an id of an artifact the GM deleted (being deleted or gone) is left out with 200 and fewer records than asked; the worker then fails the attempt for a retry, whose scope no longer holds the artifact)

Resolve the claimed job's question's terms within its scope (contract 1.23.0): the record type keys, term names and aliases, and in-scope records its words name, each by an exact match on a keyed fingerprint; no body (403 job.grant_refused, also once the job's campaign is deleted, which ends its claim; 403 job.terms_refused for a job whose kind resolves no term)

get.summary: The version of the internal API contract
